strengths: Addresses an important question: what multimodal contrastive learning recovers when modalities contain separate but dependent semantic factors and modality-specific nuisance variables.
The empirical coverage is broad, spanning synthetic distributions, CelebA, Multimodal3DIdent, four CLIP backbones, domain shifts, and few-shot adaptation across 11 datasets.

The simple postprocessing pipeline produces promising reported improvements. Synthetic MCC results and the additional ground-truth factor evaluation on Multimodal3DIdent provide useful evidence beyond classification accuracy alone.
weaknesses: A fundamental error undermines both main identifiability proofs. Lemma 2 in Appendix D.1 incorrectly claims that the normalized contrastive loss has minimum zero. Under the uniform-circle/vMF model with k=1, tau=1, and identity encoders using the cosine score, the normalized loss is approximately -0.421. Furthermore, the proof requires h_x(z_x)=h_t(z_t) almost surely; the full-support vMF joint makes this possible only for constant maps, contradicting uniformity and latent recovery. Consequently, the reduction to shared, nuisance-free encoders underlying Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 is not established.

The convex-body proof incorrectly substitutes exact uniformity for a limiting result. On a bounded interval with a truncated Laplace conditional, uniform p(z_x) generally produces nonuniform p(z_t), because the conditional normalizer varies near boundaries. Lemma 3 concerns lambda approaching zero, but Eq. (43) assumes exact uniformity at finite lambda. Corollary 2 also omits the L^alpha, alpha≠2 restriction required by its appendix proof; arbitrary norm-induced metrics do not guarantee permutation-only ambiguity.

The theoretical justification for FastICA is incompatible with the spherical assumptions. A uniform spherical distribution has dependent Cartesian components and is rotationally invariant, so ICA cannot identify its original coordinate axes. Having M−1 intrinsic dimensions does not resolve this problem. Appendix O also treats arbitrary orthogonal mixing as component-wise disentanglement, although such mixing combines factors. The proposed local-isometry/PCA argument supplies no quantitative recovery guarantee.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement from ordinary preprocessing effects. FastICA introduces whitening and dimensionality reduction, but matched PCA-only and PCA-whitening baselines are missing. This matters particularly because an orthogonal rotation of whitened features cannot change an optimally fitted L2-regularized linear probe. The reported accuracy improvements therefore do not establish that ICA's factor separation causes the gains.

Direct disentanglement validation remains insufficient. CelebA relies on selected traversals, including explicitly combined attributes such as gender/mustache. Multimodal3DIdent reports R² rather than component-wise recovery comparisons between raw CLIP, PCA, and ICA. Moreover, Appendix K regresses learned representations on true factors; high R² in this direction can coexist with rank-deficient representations and does not establish invertible latent recovery.

The causal contribution is insufficiently formalized. An undirected dependency between latent blocks does not itself specify causal or intervention semantics, and heterogeneous mechanisms do not generally preclude DAG representations with additional latent variables. The manuscript does not demonstrate that its restrictive parametric families capture the motivating mixtures of opposing mechanisms. Much of the remaining theory imports existing single-modal results, making the validity of the new cross-modal reduction especially consequential.

Reproducibility and reporting need improvement. The main few-shot tables lack uncertainty estimates; PCA/ICA fitting splits, key synthetic training settings, and the Multimodal3DIdent protocol are insufficiently specified. Table 2 also reports the RN101 baseline target average as 20.03, whereas its four entries average 22.03, overstating the corresponding improvement.
